# temper

> CSS library for plain, semantic HTML. Elements look finished without classes. Variants are
> `data-*` attributes with fixed values. Light and dark mode switch automatically.

## Setup

```js
import '@tiaforge-ui/temper/core.css';   // always
import '@tiaforge-ui/temper/app.css';    // app shell, navigation rail, floating action button
import '@tiaforge-ui/temper/menu.css';   // dropdown menus
import '@tiaforge-ui/temper/feedback.css'; // toasts, tooltips
import '@tiaforge-ui/temper/table.css';  // data tables: sortable headers, selection, number columns
import '@tiaforge-ui/temper/icons.css';  // the default icon set (see Icons)
import '@tiaforge-ui/temper/pico-compat.css'; // only while components written for Pico (reading --pico-*) remain
// or everything: import '@tiaforge-ui/temper/all.css';
```

```js
// vite.config.js: runs temper check in every build (errors fail the build, the dev server warns)
import temper from '@tiaforge-ui/temper/vite';
export default { plugins: [temper()] };
// with icons: every Lucide icon by name (only the used ones are emitted) plus your own SVG folder
// export default { plugins: [temper({ icons: { dir: 'src/icons' } })] };  and  import 'virtual:temper-icons.css';
// (then do not also import icons.css; the CLI equivalent is: npx temper check --lucide --icons src/icons <paths>)
// while migrating step by step, check only the migrated parts: temper({ paths: ['src/contacts', 'contacts'] })
// opt-in enhancements (newer CSS, fine to leave off): temper({ enhance: ['customizable-select'] }) or enhance: 'all'
// smaller builds: temper({ prune: true }) drops rules for attributes and values the project never uses
// without the plugin: import '@tiaforge-ui/temper/enhance/customizable-select.css' after core.css
```

Types for computed values (`data-tone={failed ? 'danger' : 'success'}`), checked by your framework's
type checker: reference one file once, e.g. in `src/env.d.ts`:
`/// <reference types="@tiaforge-ui/temper/react" />` (also `vue`, `astro`, `svelte`). For sinter,
add `import type {} from '@tiaforge-ui/temper/sinter';` to the sinter types module. svelte-check does
not type attributes written on elements; `temper check` checks those expressions itself.

## Rules

1. Write semantic HTML first. `button`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `label`, `fieldset`, `dialog`,
   `[popover]`, `details`, `table`, `article` (card), `dl`, `progress`, `meter`, `code`, `kbd` are styled
   without any attributes.
2. Use HTML and ARIA state, not attributes of your own: `disabled`, `aria-busy="true"` (spinner, shown after 200ms),
   `aria-invalid="true"` (error border), `aria-pressed="true"` (toggled), `aria-current`,
   `aria-selected="true"` (the selected `role="tab"`; see Tabs).
3. Variants are the `data-*` attributes listed below, with exactly the listed values. Each attribute
   is one independent axis: `data-variant` is the style, `data-tone` is the color, `data-size` is the
   size. Do not invent classes or values for these.
4. **Spacing:** nothing has an outer margin. The parent owns all space: `data-gap` between its
   children (needs `data-layout`), `data-pad` around them. Do not write `margin` or `padding` in
   `style` attributes. To add space between two things, wrap them in a `data-layout` element.
   `data-layout` overrides an element's own display, so `<label data-layout="row">` is a real row.
   `data-grow` on one child makes it take the remaining space (search fields, inputs next to a button).
5. Sizes always use the same words: `xs sm md lg xl`. There are no numeric scales.
6. Your own CSS always wins over temper (temper lives in `@layer tm.*`). Never use `!important`.
   In your own CSS, use the tokens (`var(--tm-text-muted)`, `var(--tm-space-sm)`), never hard-coded colors.
7. Use `class` only for your app's own components. `data-*` attributes from the list below belong to
   temper; do not use those names for anything else.
8. Navigations within the site cross-fade (view transitions). To turn that off, add
   `@view-transition { navigation: none; }` to your CSS; do not add your own `@view-transition` otherwise.
9. Size and tune things with the documented custom properties in `style` (`style="--tm-min: 12rem"`,
   `style="--tm-tone: #e8590c"`, `style="--tm-avatar-size: 4rem"`). That is the intended way; do not
   write `width`, `margin` or `padding` there.
10. Run `npx temper check <dir>` (`--fix` applies the safe fixes) after editing (or use the Vite plugin, which runs it in every build).
   It reports bad values, misplaced attributes, missing module imports and
   unlabeled buttons. For "no attribute" use `null`, not `false`: `cond ? 'x' : null`.
11. To see the result, prefer `npx temper-inspect <dev-server-url>` (package
    `@tiaforge-ui/temper-inspect`, if installed) over screenshots. It opens every dialog and popover
    at a wide and a narrow width, in light and dark mode, and reports overflow, misplaced overlays,
    contrast, unlabeled controls and covered click targets as text. To judge how it looks, add
    `--sheet <dir>`: one small image per page with every state at every width and scheme, plus each
    state at full size in `<dir>/<page>/` for details.

## Attributes

### `data-variant`

On: button, a[role=button], input[type=submit|button|reset]. Button style. Leave it out for the default solid main button (black in light mode, white in dark mode). Combine with data-tone for color.

- `secondary`: Tinted fill, no border. Second most important action.
- `outline`: Transparent with a border.
- `ghost`: Transparent, fill on hover. Toolbars, icon buttons, Cancel.
- `link`: Looks like a link, keeps button semantics.
- `item`: Full-width, multi-line list entry (message list, search results). Selected (aria-current, aria-selected or aria-pressed) gets a soft accent background. data-size="sm" makes a compact row (event chips).

### `data-tone`

On: button, [data-badge], [data-callout], progress, any text element. Color role. Independent of data-variant. On text it sets the text color. For a custom color use style="--tm-tone: <color>" instead.

- `accent`: The accent color (blue by default).
- `neutral`: Grey. Default for secondary/outline/ghost buttons and badges.
- `danger`: Destructive actions and errors.
- `success`: Completed or healthy states.
- `warning`: Needs attention soon.
- `info`: Neutral information. Default for callouts.

### `data-size`

On: button (also icon buttons), input, select, [data-avatar]. Control size relative to the current density.

- `sm`: 0.8× height, smaller text.
- `md`: Default size.
- `lg`: 1.2× height, larger text.

### `data-icon`

On: button, a, or any element (span) for a standalone icon. An icon by name (Lucide names). <span data-icon="mail"></span> is an icon; <button data-icon="plus">New</button> puts it before the text; an empty <button data-icon="plus" aria-label="New contact"></button> is a square icon-only button and needs an aria-label. Without a value (<button data-icon aria-label="…"><svg>…</svg></button>) it makes a square icon button around your own svg. The default set needs icons.css (or all.css); the Vite plugin makes every Lucide icon and your own SVG folder available.

Also valid without a value.

Values: `mail`, `inbox`, `send`, `calendar`, `calendar-plus`, `clock`, `users`, `user`, `user-plus`, `search`, `bell`, `settings`, `log-out`, `log-in`, `menu`, `plus`, `minus`, `x`, `check`, `pencil`, `trash-2`, `share-2`, `copy`, `download`, `upload`, `paperclip`, `link`, `external-link`, `star`, `heart`, `filter`, `refresh-cw`, `ellipsis`, `ellipsis-vertical`, `chevron-down`, `chevron-up`, `chevron-left`, `chevron-right`, `arrow-left`, `arrow-right`, `house`, `info`, `circle-alert`, `triangle-alert`, `circle-check`, `eye`, `eye-off`, `lock`, `map-pin`, `phone`, `archive`, `folder`, `file`, `image`, `sun`, `moon`.

### `data-layout`

On: any container. Lays out the element's children. Wins over the element's own display, so it also works on label, article, fieldset, dialog. Space between children comes from data-gap, space around them from data-pad; children never get margins.

- `stack`: Vertical column.
- `row`: Horizontal row, items vertically centered. Wraps onto more lines when it runs out of space, except on button, a and label (icon + text stays on one line). Override with data-wrap.
- `grid`: Responsive columns, each at least --tm-min wide (default 16rem). A few items keep their column width instead of stretching across the row.
- `split`: Sidebar + content. First child is the sidebar (--tm-split, default 16rem); wraps on narrow screens.
- `center`: Horizontally centered column with side padding. Its content is at most --tm-measure wide (default 72rem); the padding comes on top.

### `data-cols`

On: [data-layout=grid]. Exactly this many equal columns instead of responsive ones (week and month grids, a 7-day picker). Columns never wrap; use data-show to swap in another layout on phones.

Values: `2`, `3`, `4`, `5`, `6`, `7`.

### `data-gap`

On: [data-layout]. Space between the children of a data-layout element. Default md. Together with data-pad, the only spacing controls in temper.

- `none`: 0
- `xs`: 0.25rem
- `sm`: 0.5rem
- `md`: 1rem
- `lg`: 1.5rem
- `xl`: 2.5rem

### `data-pad`

On: any container: page wrappers, sections, panels, rows. Padding inside the element, on all sides. Use it instead of padding in style attributes. On data-layout="center" the side padding never drops below md. Overrides a component's own padding (e.g. data-pad="sm" on an article).

- `none`: 0
- `xs`: 0.25rem
- `sm`: 0.5rem
- `md`: 1rem
- `lg`: 1.5rem
- `xl`: 2.5rem

### `data-align`

On: [data-layout], button. Cross-axis alignment of children (align-items). A button is a flex row already, so it works there without data-layout.

Values: `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch`.

### `data-justify`

On: [data-layout], button. Main-axis distribution of children (justify-content). A button is a flex row already, so it works there without data-layout; it also aligns a label that wraps (data-justify="start" on a "From: …" toggle).

- `start`
- `center`
- `end`
- `between`: Space between the children.

### `data-self`

On: a child of data-layout (stack, row, grid). Aligns this one child across the layout, overriding data-align. Typical: an "Add" button in a stack that should not stretch to full width (data-self="start").

Values: `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch`.

### `data-wrap`

On: [data-layout=row]. Whether a row wraps onto more lines. Rows wrap by default.

- `wrap`: Default for rows.
- `none`: Keep everything on one line (nav items, icon + label).

### `data-grow` (boolean, no value)

On: a child of data-layout=row or stack. This child takes the remaining space in its row or stack (and may shrink below its content in a column, e.g. a scrolling pane). Typical: the search field in a toolbar (<input type="search" data-grow>), the input in an input + button row, the title that pushes actions to the right. It starts at --tm-grow-basis (default 8rem): with less room the row wraps and it gets its own line.

### `data-scroll`

On: a wrapper around wide or tall content (table, code, list pane). Scroll container. Without a value it scrolls sideways when the content is wider than the screen, instead of making the whole page scroll (wrap wide tables in it). data-scroll="y" scrolls vertically inside a fixed-height area (panes in a data-shell="fixed" app, message lists).

Also valid without a value.

- `y`: Vertical scrolling (panes, long lists).
- `both`: Both directions.

### `data-gutter` (boolean, no value)

On: the element that scrolls: <main> of a data-shell="fixed" page whose main scrolls, a data-scroll="y" pane, or <html> when the document scrolls. Reserves the scrollbar's space on this scroll container (scrollbar-gutter: stable), so the content does not shift sideways when it starts or stops overflowing: a tab, a filter or loaded data that makes it taller or shorter than the screen. Only classic scrollbars take space (Chrome and Edge on Linux and Windows); with overlay scrollbars nothing changes. Put it only on an element that scrolls: the space stays reserved when nothing overflows, so on a <main> that only holds panes (which scroll themselves) it leaves an empty strip at the edge.

### `data-density`

On: html or any subtree. Control height and padding for everything inside.

- `comfortable`: Default. 2.5rem controls.
- `compact`: 2rem controls, smaller text. For dense apps.

### `data-theme`

On: html or any subtree. Forces light or dark mode. Leave it out to follow the operating system.

- `light`: Always light.
- `dark`: Always dark.

### `data-badge` (boolean, no value)

On: span. Small status label (counts, tags, states). Color with data-tone or style="--tm-tone: …".

### `data-callout` (boolean, no value)

On: div, [role=alert], [role=status]. Tinted message box. Put the title in <strong>. Color with data-tone (default info).

### `data-muted` (boolean, no value)

On: any text element. Secondary text color.

### `data-truncate` (boolean, no value)

On: any element. Single line, cut off with an ellipsis.

### `data-lazy` (boolean, no value)

On: container of a long list. On the container of a long list: its rows far off screen skip layout and paint. Set --tm-lazy-h to the row height.

### `data-clamp`

On: any text element. Cuts text off after this many lines with an ellipsis (data-truncate is the one-line version).

Values: `2`, `3`.

### `data-bar` (boolean, no value)

On: any element, usually a data-variant="item" row or a card. A colored bar on the start edge in the element's tone. Event chips: <button data-variant="item" data-size="sm" data-bar style="--tm-tone: #4CAF50">.

### `data-sr-only` (boolean, no value)

On: any element. Hidden visually, still read by screen readers.

### `data-pairs` (boolean, no value)

On: dl. Shows dt/dd pairs as a two-column label/value grid.

### `data-segmented` (boolean, no value)

On: div[role=radiogroup] of <label><input type="radio">text</label>. Segmented control: a radio group drawn as a track with the checked option as a raised chip (week/month, list/grid). The radios stay in place, invisible, over their labels, so arrow keys, screen readers and taps work as on any radio group. data-size="sm" makes it as tall as a small button. Give the group an aria-label.

### `data-caption` (boolean, no value)

On: any text element. Small, semibold, muted label text: captions above values, group headings like a letter in an index.

### `data-list` (boolean, no value)

On: ul, ol or any container of rows. One bordered box whose children are rows separated by lines: settings lists, keys, devices. Each child gets padding (data-pad on a child overrides it); give a child data-layout="row" data-justify="between" for label + action rows. Card styling of article children is removed, so <article role="listitem"> rows need no extra attributes. A leading <template> child does not count as the first row.

### `data-divider` (boolean, no value)

On: any text element. A horizontal line with the element's text in the middle, e.g. <p data-divider>or</p> between two sign-in options. Empty, it is a plain line.

### `data-avatar` (boolean, no value)

On: span, div. Round avatar with initials, or an <img> child that fills it. Colored by tone (default accent); size with data-size or style="--tm-avatar-size: 4rem".

### `data-stretch` (boolean, no value)

On: the main link or button inside an article. Makes the whole card clickable through this element. Other links and buttons in the card stay clickable. Use it on the card's title link, or on a data-variant="link" button. temper keeps the element position: static and unmoved when pressed (the overlay is placed against the card); do not give it position, transform or filter yourself. While aria-busy="true" the card is not clickable and the spinner shows on the button.

### `data-shell`

On: body or the outermost app wrapper. App shell: a navigation rail ([data-rail]) next to <main>. On narrow screens (< 48rem) the rail becomes a drawer. Without a value the document scrolls; with data-shell="fixed" the shell fills the viewport and <main> scrolls inside it, for multi-pane apps (give inner panes data-scroll="y"). On a fixed-shell page whose <main> itself scrolls (a settings page), add data-gutter to <main>, so its content does not shift when the scrollbar comes and goes. Needs `app.css`.

Also valid without a value.

- `fixed`: Fills the viewport; main scrolls inside it.

### `data-rail` (boolean, no value)

On: nav inside [data-shell]. Navigation rail. It must be a direct child of [data-shell]. Children: optional <header> (brand, collapse toggle), links/buttons or a <ul> of them, optional <footer> pinned to the bottom. Items need no attributes; mark the active one with aria-current="page" (CSS cannot detect the current page). Put item text in a <span> so it can hide when collapsed. Add the popover attribute and an id to get a drawer on narrow screens (< 48rem), opened by <button popovertarget="…" data-show="narrow">; without popover the rail stays visible on narrow screens. Needs `app.css`.

### `data-collapsed` (boolean, no value)

On: [data-rail]. Icon-only rail, set in the markup (e.g. rendered by the server from a saved preference). For a toggle the user can click, use a data-rail-collapse checkbox instead. Needs `app.css`.

### `data-rail-collapse` (boolean, no value)

On: input type="checkbox" inside [data-rail] (usually in its header). Collapse toggle drawn as a chevron icon button. Checked = icon-only rail. Needs an aria-label. CSS cannot remember it across page loads: render checked from a saved preference, or save it with a few lines of script. Needs `app.css`.

### `data-rail-label` (boolean, no value)

On: any element inside [data-rail]. Hidden while the rail is collapsed (e.g. the user name in the rail footer). Needs `app.css`.

### `data-fab` (boolean, no value)

On: button. Floating action button fixed in the bottom-right corner. Combine with data-icon and an aria-label. Needs `app.css`.

### `data-show`

On: any element. Shows the element only on narrow (< 48rem) or wide screens. Needs `app.css`.

- `narrow`: Only below 48rem (e.g. the button that opens the drawer).
- `wide`: Only from 48rem.

### `data-menu` (boolean, no value)

On: [popover] (dropdown) or any container (static menu). Menu of buttons, links and checkbox labels; <hr> separates groups. On a [popover] opened via popovertarget it is placed under its button (a plain [popover] without data-menu is centered in the viewport). Needs `menu.css`.

### `data-combo` (boolean, no value)

On: a wrapper around an input and its suggestion list. Combobox: the data-menu (role="listbox", options role="option", the highlighted one aria-selected="true") inside it opens under the field. Show and hide the list from script. Needs `menu.css`.

### `data-toasts` (boolean, no value)

On: one div per page, at the end of <body> (role="status"; popover="manual" to show above modal dialogs). Toast region: fixed to the bottom corner (bottom center on phones), stacks its [data-toast] children with the newest at the bottom. Give it role="status" so screen readers announce new toasts. Optionally popover="manual": it then sits in the top layer above an open modal dialog (call showPopover() on it again after opening a dialog). Needs `feedback.css`.

### `data-toast` (boolean, no value)

On: a div inside [data-toasts]. A toast: a short message with optional actions (data-variant="link" or "ghost" buttons, data-size="sm") and a close button (data-icon="x" with aria-label). data-tone adds a colored bar. Your code appends it to [data-toasts] (it slides in) and removes it after a few seconds; set hidden first to fade it out. Use role="alert" on the toast for errors. Needs `feedback.css`.

### `data-tooltip`

On: buttons, links and any focusable element. Tooltip shown on hover (after a short delay) and keyboard focus. data-tooltip="text" shows the text; data-tooltip without a value shows the element’s aria-label, so an icon button keeps one label (aria-label="Delete" data-tooltip). The text in data-tooltip="…" is visual only; screen readers do not get it, so do not put anything there that is not also in the label or visible. In a data-rail it opens to the side and only shows while the rail is collapsed. Not for buttons that open a menu (their caret uses the same space). Needs `feedback.css`.

Value: any text, or none.

### `data-num` (boolean, no value)

On: th and td of a number column. A number cell: right-aligned with tabular figures, so digits line up. Put it on the header cell and every cell of the column (and the footer total). In a sortable header the sort arrow moves to the left. Needs `table.css`.

## Tokens

Set inputs on `:root` in your own CSS to change the theme. Use the rest in your own CSS.

### Inputs (set these)

- `--tm-hue`: Accent hue in OKLCH degrees. Default 255.
- `--tm-chroma`: Accent saturation. Default 0.19.
- `--tm-neutral-hue`: Hue the greys lean toward. Default: --tm-hue.
- `--tm-neutral-tint`: How much the greys lean toward --tm-neutral-hue. Default 0.01 (a faint lean; 0 is pure grey).
- `--tm-primary`: Tone of default buttons. Default var(--tm-neutral); var(--tm-accent) for colored main buttons.
- `--tm-radius`: Base corner radius. Default 0.5rem. The other radii derive from it.
- `--tm-badge-radius`: Badge corner radius. Default 0.67 × --tm-radius; var(--tm-radius-full) for pills.
- `--tm-font-sans`: UI font stack. Default: system fonts.
- `--tm-font-mono`: Code font stack.
- `--tm-heading-weight`: Heading font weight. Default 600.
- `--tm-heading-tracking`: Heading letter spacing. Default -0.025em.
- `--tm-duration`: Transition duration. Default 150ms.
- `--tm-busy-delay`: How long an element is aria-busy before its spinner shows and its content dims, so a fast request shows nothing. Default 200ms.
- `--tm-ease`: Transition easing.
- `--tm-min`: Minimum column width for data-layout="grid". Default 16rem.
- `--tm-split`: Sidebar width for data-layout="split". Default 16rem.
- `--tm-measure`: Max width for data-layout="center". Default 72rem.
- `--tm-lazy-h`: Row height guess for data-lazy, until a row has been shown. Default 3rem.
- `--tm-dialog-width`: Dialog width. Default 30rem.
- `--tm-avatar-size`: Avatar diameter. Default 2.5rem (scaled by data-size).
- `--tm-rail-width`: Width of [data-rail]. Default 15rem.
- `--tm-rail-width-collapsed`: Width of a collapsed rail. Default: one icon button plus padding.
- `--tm-grow-basis`: Width a data-grow child needs before its row wraps. Default 8rem.
- `--tm-icon-<name>`: The icon image for data-icon="<name>", as a url() of an SVG (shape only; the color is the text color). Set it to replace a default icon or to add your own: :root { --tm-icon-rocket: url(/icons/rocket.svg); } plus [data-icon="rocket"] { --_icon: var(--tm-icon-rocket); }.

### Colors

- `--tm-bg`: Page background.
- `--tm-surface`: Cards, panes, inputs.
- `--tm-surface-raised`: Dialogs, popovers, menus.
- `--tm-fill`: Subtle fill: code, hover, neutral secondary buttons.
- `--tm-field`: Input background.
- `--tm-field-border`: Input border.
- `--tm-border`: Default hairline borders and dividers.
- `--tm-border-strong`: Stronger borders: inputs, outline buttons.
- `--tm-text`: Body text.
- `--tm-text-muted`: Secondary text.
- `--tm-accent`: Accent: selection, focus, links, checked controls.
- `--tm-neutral`: Neutral tone (near-black in light mode, near-white in dark mode).
- `--tm-danger`: Danger tone.
- `--tm-success`: Success tone.
- `--tm-warning`: Warning tone.
- `--tm-info`: Info tone.
- `--tm-tone`: Current tone. Set it to any color to recolor an element and its children (e.g. calendar colors).
- `--tm-tone-ink`: Text-safe version of --tm-tone. (derived, read only)
- `--tm-tone-soft`: Tinted background from --tm-tone. (derived, read only)
- `--tm-tone-on`: Text color on a solid --tm-tone fill (black or white). (derived, read only)

### Space

- `--tm-space-none`: 0
- `--tm-space-xs`: 0.25rem
- `--tm-space-sm`: 0.5rem
- `--tm-space-md`: 1rem
- `--tm-space-lg`: 1.5rem
- `--tm-space-xl`: 2.5rem

### Radius

- `--tm-radius-sm`: 0.6 × --tm-radius (derived, read only)
- `--tm-radius-lg`: 1.5 × --tm-radius. Cards and dialogs. (derived, read only)
- `--tm-radius-full`: Fully round.

### Text sizes

- `--tm-text-xs`: 0.75rem
- `--tm-text-sm`: 0.875rem
- `--tm-text-md`: 1rem
- `--tm-text-lg`: 1.25rem
- `--tm-text-xl`: 1.75rem

### Shadows

- `--tm-shadow-sm`: Resting shadow (none in the default look).
- `--tm-shadow-lg`: Overlay shadow: dialogs, popovers.

### Density (read only)

- `--tm-control-h`: Height of buttons and inputs, set by data-density. (derived, read only)
- `--tm-control-px`: Horizontal padding of controls, set by data-density. (derived, read only)
- `--tm-control-font`: Font size of controls, set by data-density. (derived, read only)

## Icons

```html
<span data-icon="mail"></span>                                        <!-- an icon, 1.125em, in the text color -->
<button data-icon="pencil">Edit</button>                              <!-- icon before the text -->
<button data-icon="x" data-variant="ghost" aria-label="Close"></button>  <!-- empty: square icon-only button, needs aria-label -->
<a href="/mail/" data-icon="mail"><span>Mail</span></a>               <!-- rail items, links -->
```

Names are Lucide's (https://lucide.dev/icons). icons.css contains: mail, inbox, send, calendar, calendar-plus, clock, users, user, user-plus, search, bell, settings, log-out, log-in, menu, plus, minus, x, check, pencil, trash-2, share-2, copy, download, upload, paperclip, link, external-link, star, heart, filter, refresh-cw, ellipsis, ellipsis-vertical, chevron-down, chevron-up, chevron-left, chevron-right, arrow-left, arrow-right, house, info, circle-alert, triangle-alert, circle-check, eye, eye-off, lock, map-pin, phone, archive, folder, file, image, sun, moon. With the Vite plugin's `icons` option every Lucide name works, and only the icons you
use end up in the CSS. Do not paste inline `<svg>` for an icon that has a name.

Your own icons: put SVG files in the plugin's `icons.dir` (file name = icon name; it replaces a default
of the same name), or without the plugin:

```css
:root { --tm-icon-mail: url(/icons/mail.svg); }            /* replace a default icon */
:root { --tm-icon-rocket: url(/icons/rocket.svg); }         /* add one */
[data-icon="rocket"] { --_icon: var(--tm-icon-rocket); }
```

Icons are one color (the text color); keep multicolor logos as `<img>`.

## Recipes

### Form

```html
<form data-layout="stack" data-gap="md">
  <label>Name <input name="name" required></label>
  <div data-layout="grid" data-gap="sm" style="--tm-min: 10rem">
    <label>Start <input type="date"></label>
    <label>Time <input type="time"></label>
  </div>
  <label>Calendar <select><option>Work</option></select></label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" role="switch"> All day</label>
  <label>Email
    <input type="email" aria-invalid="true">
    <small data-tone="danger">Enter a full address, like name@example.com.</small>
  </label>
  <div data-layout="row" data-gap="sm" data-justify="end">
    <button type="button" data-variant="ghost">Cancel</button>
    <button>Save</button>
  </div>
</form>
```

### Card

```html
<article data-layout="stack" data-gap="sm">
  <header><h3>Title</h3><button data-icon="x" data-variant="ghost" aria-label="Close"></button></header>
  <p>Body text.</p>
  <footer><button data-variant="secondary">Edit</button></footer>
</article>
```

`article > header` puts its children in a row with space between. `article > footer` aligns its
buttons to the end.

### Dialog

```html
<button commandfor="confirm" command="show-modal" data-tone="danger">Delete…</button>
<dialog id="confirm">
  <header>
    <h2>Delete “Team retro”?</h2>
    <button commandfor="confirm" command="close" aria-label="Close"></button>
  </header>
  <p>This sends a cancellation to all guests.</p>
  <footer>
    <button commandfor="confirm" command="close" data-variant="ghost">Keep</button>
    <button data-tone="danger">Delete event</button>
  </footer>
</dialog>
```

The open dialog is a grid with a gap between its direct children, so content inside a wrapper element
loses that gap. To let one part fill the remaining height (a message body, a long list), give the dialog
`data-layout="stack"` and that part `data-grow data-scroll="y"`. Pico-style `dialog > article` markup
works too: the article adds no box of its own.

Add `closedby="any"` to close the dialog on a click outside it or on Esc, with no script (no backdrop
click handlers).

An empty close button in the header (`command="close"`, `command="hide-popover"` or
`popovertargetaction="hide"`) is drawn as a quiet × icon button; give it an `aria-label`. Header and
footer also work through one wrapper (`dialog > form > footer`, a template-rendered `div`). The open
dialog is a grid with a gap between its children, so an empty helper element inside it adds an empty
row: give such elements the `hidden` attribute.

### Toolbar

```html
<div data-layout="row" data-gap="sm">
  <h2>Contacts</h2>
  <input type="search" data-grow placeholder="Search" aria-label="Search">
  <button data-icon="plus" data-variant="ghost" aria-label="Add contact"></button>
</div>
```

`data-grow` makes the search field fill the space between the heading and the button. A button whose
label does not fit (a long translation on a phone) wraps the label onto two lines; nothing to add. For a fixed
width instead, leave `data-grow` out and add `data-justify="between"` to the row.

### Status

```html
<span data-badge data-tone="success">Synced</span>
<span data-badge style="--tm-tone: #e8590c">Custom color</span>
<div data-callout data-tone="warning" role="status"><strong>Password expires soon</strong>Update it before 1 December.</div>
<button aria-busy="true">Saving</button>
```

### Settings rows

```html
<div data-layout="stack" data-gap="none" data-density="compact">
  <label data-layout="row" data-justify="between" data-pad="sm">Email notifications <input type="checkbox" role="switch"></label>
  <label data-layout="row" data-justify="between" data-pad="sm">Show week numbers <input type="checkbox" role="switch"></label>
</div>
```

### Bordered list

```html
<ul data-list>
  <li data-layout="row" data-justify="between">
    <span data-grow>Firefox on Linux <span data-badge data-tone="accent">This browser</span></span>
    <button data-icon="trash-2" data-variant="ghost" data-size="sm" data-tone="danger" aria-label="Remove"></button>
  </li>
  <li data-layout="row" data-justify="between">…</li>
</ul>
```

`data-list` draws one box with a line between rows and pads each row. `data-grow` on the label keeps
the button at the end of the row on narrow screens. Do not build the same from bordered `article`s
with `data-pad`.

### Tabs

```html
<div role="tablist" aria-label="Settings">
  <button role="tab" aria-selected="true" aria-controls="general">General</button>
  <button role="tab" aria-selected="false" aria-controls="encryption">Encryption</button>
</div>
<section role="tabpanel" id="general">…</section>
<section role="tabpanel" id="encryption" hidden>…</section>
```

No `data-variant` on tabs: the selected one (`aria-selected="true"`) is underlined. Your script switches
`aria-selected` and `hidden`. `aria-orientation="vertical"` on the tablist stacks the tabs.

### Segmented control

```html
<div role="radiogroup" data-segmented data-size="sm" aria-label="View">
  <label><input type="radio" name="view" value="week" checked>Week</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="view" value="month">Month</label>
</div>
```

A radio group for a view switch (a few short options, one always chosen). The checked label is a raised
chip; keep the `input` inside its `label`. For panels that show and hide use tabs instead.

### Divider with text

```html
<button data-variant="secondary">Sign in with a passkey</button>
<p data-divider>or</p>
```

### App shell with navigation rail (app.css)

```html
<body data-shell>
  <nav data-rail popover id="rail" aria-label="Main">
    <header>
      <span data-rail-label>Caley</span>
      <input type="checkbox" data-rail-collapse aria-label="Collapse menu">
    </header>
    <a href="/mail/" data-icon="mail"><span>Mail</span><span data-badge data-tone="accent">12</span></a>
    <a href="/contacts/" data-icon="users" aria-current="page"><span>Contacts</span></a>
    <footer>
      <span data-caption data-rail-label>Tia Heinrich</span>
      <a href="/settings/" data-icon="settings"><span>Settings</span></a>
    </footer>
  </nav>
  <main data-layout="stack" data-gap="lg" data-pad="lg">
    <div data-layout="row" data-gap="sm">
      <button popovertarget="rail" data-show="narrow" data-icon="menu" data-variant="ghost" aria-label="Open menu"></button>
      <h1>Contacts</h1>
      …
    </div>
    …
  </main>
  <button data-fab data-icon="plus" aria-label="New contact"></button>
</body>
```

No script needed. On wide screens the rail sits next to `main`, and the checkbox collapses it to icons.
Below 48rem the rail is a drawer: the ☰ button opens it, and Esc or a click outside closes it. Put
the ☰ button first in each page's top row, where it takes its own space; it is hidden on wide screens. Other
children of `data-shell` (scripts, templates, framework elements) take no space. `aria-current` must
be set in the markup; CSS cannot detect the current page.

With `data-shell="fixed"` the shell fills the viewport and `<main>` scrolls inside it (multi-pane apps: give the
panes `data-scroll="y"`). A page of such an app whose `<main>` itself scrolls (settings, a long form) gets
`<main data-gutter>`: with classic scrollbars (Chrome and Edge on Linux and Windows) its content then keeps its
place when a tab or loaded data makes it shorter or taller than the screen. Not on a `<main>` that only holds
panes: the reserved space would stay there as an empty strip.

`[data-rail]` must be a direct child of `[data-shell]` (no wrapper element in between). When an app
moves to temper page by page, keep the old nav partial for the old pages and add a second one with
this markup for the migrated pages; delete the old one when the last page has moved.

To keep the collapsed state across page loads, add this (CSS cannot store anything):

```js
const c = document.querySelector('[data-rail-collapse]');
c.checked = localStorage.getItem('rail-collapsed') === '1';
c.addEventListener('change', () => localStorage.setItem('rail-collapsed', c.checked ? '1' : '0'));
```

### Dropdown menu (menu.css)

```html
<button popovertarget="book-menu" data-variant="outline">Address books</button>
<div popover id="book-menu" data-menu>
  <label><input type="checkbox" checked> Personal</label>
  <label><input type="checkbox"> Work</label>
  <hr>
  <button>Manage address books</button>
</div>
```

Buttons that open a popover (`popovertarget`, `command="toggle-popover"`) get a ▾ caret automatically;
icon buttons (`data-icon`) do not. A submit button (`type="submit"`, the default inside a form) ignores
`popovertarget` and `commandfor`; give opener and closer buttons `type="button"`.

A `data-menu` popover can hold any content, not only items: a month picker, a small form.

### Toasts and tooltips (feedback.css)

```html
<button data-variant="ghost" data-icon="trash-2" aria-label="Delete" data-tooltip></button>  <!-- tooltip = aria-label -->
<span data-badge tabindex="0" data-tooltip="Synced 3 hours ago">Stale</span>              <!-- own text (visual only) -->

<div data-toasts role="status"></div>   <!-- once, at the end of <body> -->
```

```js
// Show a toast: append it to the region, remove it after a few seconds (hidden first, so it fades out).
function toast(text, tone) {
  const t = document.createElement('div');
  t.dataset.toast = '';
  if (tone) t.dataset.tone = tone;           // success, danger, … colors the bar
  if (tone === 'danger') t.role = 'alert';
  t.textContent = text;                       // or: a <span> plus <button data-variant="link" data-size="sm">Undo</button>
  document.querySelector('[data-toasts]').append(t);
  setTimeout(() => { t.hidden = true; setTimeout(() => t.remove(), 300); }, 5000);
}
```

In a framework, render the region once and the toasts from a list (`{#each toasts as t (t.id)}<div data-toast …>`).
To show toasts above an open modal dialog, give the region `popover="manual"` and call `region.showPopover()`
after the dialog opens (the top layer stacks in opening order).

### Data table (table.css)

```html
<div data-scroll>                       <!-- scrolls sideways on phones; data-scroll="y" + a height for a fixed header area -->
  <table>
    <caption>Invoices</caption>
    <thead><tr>
      <th><input type="checkbox" aria-label="Select all"></th>
      <th aria-sort="ascending"><button>Customer</button></th>   <!-- your code sorts, then sets aria-sort -->
      <th aria-sort="none"><button>Status</button></th>
      <th data-num aria-sort="none"><button>Amount</button></th>
      <th><span data-sr-only>Actions</span></th>
    </tr></thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <td><input type="checkbox" aria-label="Select Acme" checked></td>   <!-- checked: the row is highlighted -->
        <th scope="row">Acme Corp</th>
        <td><span data-badge data-tone="success">Paid</span></td>
        <td data-num>1,204.50</td>
        <td><div data-layout="row" data-gap="xs" data-justify="end">
          <button data-variant="ghost" data-size="sm" data-icon="pencil" aria-label="Edit"></button>
        </div></td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
    <tfoot><tr><td></td><th scope="row" colspan="2">Total</th><td data-num>1,204.50</td><td></td></tr></tfoot>
  </table>
</div>
```

The header sticks while the page scrolls. Put `data-num` on every cell of a number column. Never put
`data-layout` on a `td` (it stops being a cell); wrap the cell content instead. No rows: one
`<tr><td colspan="5" data-muted>No invoices yet.</td></tr>`.

### Combobox (menu.css)

```html
<div data-combo>
  <input type="text" role="combobox" aria-label="To" aria-controls="to-list" aria-expanded="true">
  <div data-menu role="listbox" id="to-list">
    <div role="option" aria-selected="true">Priya Raman &lt;priya@raman.dev&gt;</div>
    <div role="option">Mira Okafor &lt;mira@okafor.io&gt;</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

Show and hide the list, and move `aria-selected` with the arrow keys, from script.

### Calendar grid and event chips

```html
<div data-layout="grid" data-cols="7" data-gap="xs">
  <div data-layout="stack" data-gap="xs">
    <span data-caption aria-current="date">Sat 7</span>
    <button data-variant="item" data-size="sm" data-bar style="--tm-tone: #4CAF50">
      <small data-muted>10:00</small><span data-clamp="2">Market and brunch</span>
    </button>
  </div>
  …
</div>
```

### Card grid with avatars, whole card clickable

```html
<div data-layout="grid" data-gap="md" style="--tm-min: 13rem">
  <article data-layout="stack" data-gap="xs" data-align="center">
    <span data-avatar>MO</span>
    <a href="#mira" data-stretch><strong>Mira Okafor</strong></a>
    <!-- or, when a click opens a dialog: <button data-stretch data-variant="link" commandfor="detail" command="show-modal">Mira Okafor</button> -->
    <a href="mailto:mira@okafor.io">mira@okafor.io</a>
    <small data-muted>Climbing club</small>
  </article>
</div>
```

### Label/value pairs

```html
<dl data-pairs>
  <dt>From</dt><dd>Priya Raman</dd>
  <div data-sn-show="c.phone"><dt>Phone</dt><dd>+49 30 9876 5432</dd></div>
</dl>
```

A `div` around a `dt`/`dd` pair is allowed (to show or hide the pair as one).

### Page layout

```html
<main data-layout="center" data-gap="xl" data-pad="xl">
  <section data-layout="stack" data-gap="md">…</section>
  <section data-layout="grid" data-gap="lg" style="--tm-min: 20rem">…</section>
</main>
```

## Anti-patterns

| Don't | Do |
|---|---|
| `<button class="secondary">` | `<button data-variant="secondary">` |
| `<button data-variant="danger">` | `<button data-tone="danger">` (tone is color, variant is style) |
| `<button data-variant="primary">` | `<button>` (primary is the default) |
| `<p class="error">` | `<p data-tone="danger">` or `<div data-callout data-tone="danger">` |
| `style="margin-top: 1rem"` on a button or input | wrap the elements in `data-layout="stack" data-gap="md"` |
| `style="padding: var(--tm-space-lg)"` | `data-pad="lg"` |
| a custom class to turn a `label` into a flex row | `<label data-layout="row" data-justify="between">` |
| `data-gap="4"` or `data-gap="16px"` | `data-gap="md"` |
| `<button data-icon="x"></button>` | `<button data-icon="x" aria-label="Close"></button>` |
| `<svg><path d="…"/></svg>` for a mail icon | `<span data-icon="mail"></span>` |
| `data-badge="true"` | `data-badge` |
| `color: #666` in app CSS | `color: var(--tm-text-muted)` |
| `!important` to beat temper | a plain selector; app CSS already wins |
